name: CAMBODIA

flag.title: Flag of Cambodia
flag.note: Red centre, blue edges; Angkor Wat in white

lead: Cambodia is in the heart of Southeast Asia. The Mekong River flows past jungles that hide Angkor Wat, one of the world's greatest wonders. The Khmer people built a huge empire here over a thousand years ago.
geo: Cambodia is mostly flat lowlands watered by the Mekong River. Tonle Sap, Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake, swells to six times its dry-season size when monsoon floods reverse its river.
The Cardamom Mountains rise in the southwest and shelter dense rainforest. About 20% of the land is farmed, mostly rice paddies.
animals: The Irrawaddy dolphin is chubby and looks like it is smiling. It lives in a short stretch of the Mekong near Kratie. About 100 survive, and Cambodians see them as sacred.
The giant ibis, Cambodia's national bird, is nearly as tall as a child. It is critically endangered and nests in northern forests.
culture: Cambodians greet each other with a sampeah. They press their palms together and bow a little. The higher the hands, the more respect they show.
Khmer food is built around prahok, a fermented fish paste nicknamed 'Cambodian cheese'. Fish amok, steamed in banana leaves with coconut milk, is the dish visitors remember most.
history: In 802 CE, King Jayavarman II declared himself god-king and began the Khmer Empire. Over 600 years, it grew to cover much of mainland Southeast Asia. Its capital, Angkor, became the largest pre-industrial city on Earth.
Thai invaders ended the empire in 1431. Cambodia later became a French colony. In the 1970s, the Khmer Rouge caused terrible loss of life.
wows: Angkor Wat covers 162 hectares and has a moat over 5 km around it.
Cambodia's flag shows the towers of Angkor Wat.
The Tonle Sap River reverses direction twice a year.
At its 13th-century peak, Angkor was as wide as modern Los Angeles.
Cambodia has no McDonald's, one of the last in Southeast Asia without one.
Khmer is not a tonal language.
Cambodian weddings last three full days, so every relative can celebrate.

myths.myth: Angkor Wat was a lost city forgotten for centuries
myths.fact: People kept living and praying there. European explorers made it famous abroad in the 1800s.

myths.myth: Angkor Wat was always a Buddhist temple
myths.fact: King Suryavarman II built it for the Hindu god Vishnu in the early 1100s. It became Buddhist later.
